item.text: The initial read returned `not_found`, so I initialized this project from the supplied snapshot. The assurance view preserves both identity claims and flags their disagreement as blocking. The JV note does not establish the physical DUT’s identity; the JW-based electrical conclusions remain conditional.

actions.summary: Obtain physical marking/package evidence and traceable order record; reconcile JW/JV claims while retaining provenance; obtain matching package-specific documentation.
Identify programmer and document loaded logic levels, supported SPI modes, clock and timing behavior. No measurements are currently attached.
Select translator orderable package and verify pin numbers, footprint, availability and assembly constraints; revisit candidate and rail selection against resolved DUT.
Close VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL and worst-case propagation, setup/hold and load budget; derive supported clock rather than assume one.
Define actual supply implementation, current budget, sequencing, decoupling, protection, OE startup/shutdown and unused-pin handling.
Create and review schematic/ERC and PCB/DRC against resolved packages and mapping.
Prepare later independently authorized physical validation for rails, sequencing, loaded levels and SPI timing. No fabrication or power-on authorization is granted here.

architecture_candidates.rationale: For declared JW at 1.8 V, pin maximum is 2.2 V; 3.3 V exceeds it (and exceeds 2.35 V at maximum operating VCC). Absolute maximum is not a normal operating target. No supported direct connection for the unresolved physical DUT.

Conditional on JW standard SPI: three forward and one reverse channel match. VCCA=3.3 V host, VCCB=1.8 V DUT are within declared translator ranges. Physical implementation held; thresholds, timing, pin numbers, supply circuit and identity are unresolved.

One device with uniform host A / DUT B assignment cannot provide simultaneous 3-forward/1-reverse using two shared-direction two-bit groups. Supply range fits but does not resolve topology. This rejection is limited to that arrangement, not every possible multi-device or mixed-side design.

blockers: Exact physical DUT marking, package, orderable suffix, and package-specific pinout.
